title: Land needs study and planning fee review
subtitle: Elora Meadows rink pad, heritage approvals, sponsorship program, community grants, animal control extension and advisory board appointments.
overview: Council agreed to hire Watson & Associates Economists to prepare a Community Land Needs Assessment, with a required scenario of 30% intensification and 55 people and jobs per hectare. Staff said expanding the urban boundary would take agricultural land, so higher density is one way to reduce that. Council also accepted a planning and development fee study and directed staff to prepare a fees by-law amendment. Staff want to move from about 75% cost recovery toward full cost recovery, which means planning fees are likely to rise.

Council supported a neighbourhood group's plan for an outdoor multi-use pad at Elora Meadows Park and will receive an agreement later. It approved a partial demolition at 244 Melville Street and a heritage permit for 27-43 West Mill Street in Elora. It adopted a sponsorship and naming rights program and a new Community Impact Grant policy, and extended animal control service to June 30, 2023.
Council also made board appointments and approved drain maintenance by-laws. The termite management update was deferred because of new information, and staff plan to bring it back later.

decisions.detail: Council authorized staff to retain Watson & Associates Economists for the assessment, with a scenario of 30% intensification and 55 people and jobs per hectare added by amendment.
Council accepted the Watson & Associates fee study and told staff to prepare an amendment to the Fees and Charges By-law.
Council supported the concept plan, authorized a letter of support from the Mayor and directed staff to draft an agreement with the Elora Meadows Association.
Council adopted the sponsorship and naming rights program in-house, amended the 2023 fees schedule and delegated authority to the Managing Director of Community Services and the CAO.
Council adopted the Community Impact Grant Policy and pre-approved the 2023 annual specific grants listed in Schedule A.
Council approved Heritage Permit HP2023-001 for alterations to 27-43 West Mill Street, Elora, subject to six conditions.
Council approved demolition of the tower and rear addition at the listed property, which stays on the Municipal Heritage Register.
Council authorized an extension of animal control and shelter services with the Guelph Humane Society, in partnership with Guelph-Eramosa, to June 30, 2023.

debate: A resident delegate supported the land needs study but asked that its terms of reference be made public and that community and heritage groups take part. The delegate also objected to February 22 public meetings on building height zoning changes, saying they came ahead of the study and might need an Official Plan Amendment.

One councillor said growth needs services such as daycare, citing a long wait list. Another asked whether scenarios with higher intensification for Centre Wellington had been tested. Staff said the County's figures came from limits such as heritage resources and servicing, and that the Province can overrule local decisions on land supply.

On the fee study, consultants said planning fees currently recover well under half of costs, and the study assumes added staff positions. A councillor welcomed new parks fees as helpful to groups fundraising for parks.

On the Elora Meadows pad, councillors asked about fence height and distance to homes, and about fairness for neighbourhoods with less fundraising capacity. Staff said the pad exceeds the standard neighbourhood park build, and other groups can approach the department. Staff said any fee waiver would be Council's decision.
On the sponsorship program, one councillor asked that signage in natural spaces be limited. Staff pointed to policy wording requiring sponsorships to fit the Township's values and public image.
